The present disclosure provides a dispenser for pressurized material. In an embodiment, the dispenser for pressurized material includes a container half having an exposed edge and a closure member at the exposed edge. The container half has a cup half in an interior top portion. The dispenser includes a reciprocal container half having a reciprocal exposed edge and a reciprocal closure member at the reciprocal exposed edge. The reciprocal container half has a reciprocal cup half in an interior top portion. The closure member and the reciprocal closure member matingly engage along the exposed edges to attach the container half to the reciprocal container half and form a container. The dispenser includes a sleeve bag on valve (SBoV) assembly in an interior of the container. The SBoV assembly includes a valve seat. The cup and the reciprocal cup support the valve seat to secure the SBoV assembly in the container.

The disclosure describes a dispenser configured to contain and dispense pressurized material. The dispenser includes two complementary container halves, each having an exposed edge, a closure member, and an interior cup half. The closure members matingly engage along the exposed edges to connect the two container halves and form an assembled container.

A sleeve bag-on-valve (SBoV) assembly, including a valve seat, is positioned within the assembled container. The interior cup halves cooperate to support the valve seat and retain the SBoV assembly securely in place within the container.
outputs.L4:
The disclosure relates to a dispenser for storing and dispensing a pressurized material. The dispenser includes a container body formed from first and second container halves that are joined together during assembly. Each container half defines a corresponding portion of the container interior and includes an inwardly projecting cup half. When the two container halves are mated, the cup halves cooperate to form a support structure within the assembled container.

A sleeve bag-on-valve (SBoV) assembly is positioned between the container halves before they are joined. The SBoV assembly includes a flexible sleeve or bag for containing the material to be dispensed and a valve assembly having a valve seat. As the container halves are brought together, their respective cup halves surround and engage the valve-seat region of the SBoV assembly. In the assembled dispenser, the combined cup halves support the valve seat and constrain its movement relative to the container body.

This arrangement securely retains the SBoV assembly within the container without requiring the valve seat to be supported by only one of the container halves. Loads applied to the valve during filling, storage, handling, or dispensing can instead be transferred through the cooperating cup halves to the assembled container body. The resulting structure helps maintain the position and alignment of the valve assembly while reducing the likelihood that the SBoV assembly will shift or become dislodged.

To assemble the dispenser, the SBoV assembly is placed in one container half with the valve-seat region received by that half’s interior cup portion. The second container half is then positioned over the assembly so that its cup portion engages the opposite side of the valve-seat region. The container halves are subsequently secured together, thereby completing both the external container and the internal support surrounding the valve seat. Once assembled and pressurized, actuation of the valve permits the material held in the sleeve or bag to be discharged through the valve while the cooperating cup halves continue to retain and support the SBoV assembly.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a dispenser for pressurized material made from two mating container halves that support a sleeve bag-on-valve assembly.
counterfactuals.output: A dispenser for pressurized material includes first and second container halves configured to mate along respective peripheral interfaces to define an internal pressure chamber. The container halves cooperatively support a sleeve bag-on-valve assembly comprising a flexible bag for containing a dispensable material, a valve coupled to the bag, and a sleeve surrounding at least a portion of the bag. Retention features formed in one or both container halves engage the sleeve and/or valve to locate and secure the assembly within the pressure chamber. A propellant introduced into a space between the flexible bag and the container halves applies pressure to the bag, thereby dispensing material through the valve when the valve is actuated. The mating container halves facilitate installation of the sleeve bag-on-valve assembly and may be joined by mechanical engagement, welding, bonding, or a combination thereof to provide a pressure-resistant enclosure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

A pressurized-material dispensing apparatus comprising:

a housing including a first housing portion and a second housing portion removably attachable to one another, each of the first and second housing portions defining an upper interior cup portion; and

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an exemplary embodiment for a patent application covering a two-piece container with mating edge closures and an internally secured sleeve bag on valve assembly.
counterfactuals.output:
## Exemplary Embodiment

Referring to FIGS. 1–6, a container assembly 100 includes a first container portion 110, a second container portion 120, an internal flexible sleeve bag 140, and a valve assembly 160. The first and second container portions 110, 120 are joinable along respective peripheral edges to form a substantially enclosed, pressure-resistant outer container 102. The sleeve bag 140 is positioned within the outer container 102 and is secured internally to the valve assembly 160 such that contents of the sleeve bag 140 may be dispensed through the valve assembly 160 while remaining isolated from the outer container 102.

The first container portion 110 may define an upper shell and the second container portion 120 may define a lower shell. In other embodiments, the portions 110, 120 may be left and right shells or otherwise divided along a transverse, longitudinal, or non-planar parting line. Each portion may be molded, stamped, cast, thermoformed, or otherwise formed from metal, polymer, fiber-reinforced material, or a combination thereof.

The first container portion 110 includes a first body wall 112 terminating at a first peripheral edge 114. A first mating closure feature 116 extends along at least part of the first peripheral edge 114. The second container portion 120 similarly includes a second body wall 122 terminating at a second peripheral edge 124, along which a second mating closure feature 126 is provided. The first and second mating closure features 116, 126 are complementary and engage one another when the container portions 110, 120 are brought together.

In the illustrated embodiment, the first mating closure feature 116 includes an outwardly projecting rib or bead 117, and the second mating closure feature 126 includes a complementary channel 127 configured to receive the rib 117. The rib 117 and channel 127 may extend continuously around the respective peripheral edges 114, 124. Engagement of the rib 117 with the channel 127 aligns the container portions, resists relative lateral displacement, and forms a mechanical edge closure. The mating closure features may establish an interference fit, snap fit, dovetail fit, rolled-seam engagement, tongue-and-groove engagement, or other releasable or permanent interconnection.

A sealing member 130 may be positioned between the first and second peripheral edges 114, 124. The sealing member 130 may comprise an elastomeric gasket, O-ring, molded sealing lip, adhesive layer, weld bead, or curable sealant. In one example, the sealing member 130 is received in an annular groove 128 formed adjacent the channel 127 and is compressed by a sealing land 118 of the first container portion 110 as the mating closure features 116, 126 are engaged. The closure thereby limits leakage of gas or liquid through the interface between the container portions.

The edge closure may be retained by one or more retaining elements 132. The retaining elements 132 may include circumferential bands, clamps, latches, threaded collars, crimped regions, fasteners, welds, adhesives, or combinations thereof. In one embodiment, a removable clamp band surrounds outwardly extending flanges adjacent the peripheral edges 114, 124, thereby permitting the container portions to be separated for insertion or replacement of the sleeve bag 140. In another embodiment, the mating closure features are permanently joined by ultrasonic welding, laser welding, solvent bonding, induction welding, or mechanical crimping.

The sleeve bag 140 includes a flexible wall 142 defining a product chamber 144. The flexible wall 142 may be formed as an elongated tubular sleeve having a closed distal end 146 and an open proximal end 148. The distal end 146 may be closed by a transverse heat seal, fold seal, weld, adhesive bond, mechanical clip, or an integrally formed end wall. The flexible wall 142 may comprise a monolayer or multilayer polymer film selected to provide desired barrier, chemical-resistance, sterilization, and flexibility properties. Suitable materials may include polyethylene, polypropylene, polyamide, polyester, ethylene-vinyl alcohol, fluoropolymer, metallized film, or laminates thereof.

The valve assembly 160 is mounted in an opening 134 formed through the first container portion 110. The valve assembly 160 includes a valve body 162 having an external dispensing portion 164 and an internal coupling portion 166. A mounting flange 168 extends from the valve body 162 and engages an exterior or interior surface of the first body wall 112. A valve seal 170 is positioned between the mounting flange 168 and the first container portion 110. A retaining member 172, such as a threaded nut, snap ring, crimp ring, bayonet retainer, or welded collar, secures the valve body 162 to the first container portion 110.

A fluid passage 174 extends through the valve body 162 between an internal inlet 176 and an external outlet 178. A selectively operable valve element 180 is disposed in the fluid passage 174. The valve element 180 may comprise a poppet, stem, diaphragm, duckbill, slit valve, ball valve, or other normally closed or selectively actuated flow-control member. The external dispensing portion 164 may be configured for direct dispensing or for connection to a dispensing head, hose, faucet, pump, or pressurized dispensing apparatus.

The open proximal end 148 of the sleeve bag 140 is secured to the internal coupling portion 166 of the valve assembly 160. In the illustrated embodiment, the internal coupling portion 166 includes an annular spigot 182 projecting into the outer container 102. The open proximal end 148 is fitted over the spigot 182, and an annular securing member 184 compresses the flexible wall 142 against the spigot 182. The securing member 184 may comprise a crimp ring, clamp, elastic collar, threaded compression ring, heat-shrink member, snap-fit collar, weld, or adhesive bond.

The spigot 182 may include one or more circumferential retention barbs 186 that resist withdrawal of the sleeve bag 140. A sealing surface 188 positioned between or adjacent the retention barbs 186 engages the inner surface of the sleeve bag 140 to form a fluid-tight connection. In certain embodiments, the securing member 184 is located entirely inside the outer container 102 after assembly. Thus, the bag-to-valve connection is protected by the first and second container portions and is inaccessible during ordinary use.

Alternatively, the proximal end 148 may include a fitment 190 welded or bonded to the flexible wall 142. The fitment 190 may be connected to the internal coupling portion 166 by complementary threads, a bayonet connection, a snap fit, a press fit, or a welded joint. A gasket may be positioned between the fitment 190 and the valve body 162. The fitment embodiment permits the sleeve bag 140 to be attached to the valve assembly 160 before the container portions are joined.

During assembly, the valve assembly 160 is mounted to the first container portion 110. The proximal end 148 of the sleeve bag 140 is then secured to the internal coupling portion 166, with the product chamber 144 in fluid communication with the inlet 176 of the valve assembly. The sleeve bag 140 is folded, rolled, pleated, or otherwise arranged within one of the container portions. The first and second container portions 110, 120 are brought together so that the first and second mating closure features 116, 126 engage. The sealing member 130 is compressed, and the retaining elements 132 are applied to maintain the container portions in the assembled condition.

The sleeve bag 140 may be filled before closure of the two container portions, through the valve assembly 160 after closure, or through a separate fill port that is subsequently sealed. When the valve assembly 160 is actuated, product exits the product chamber 144 through the fluid passage 174. As product is discharged, the flexible wall 142 collapses inwardly, thereby reducing the volume of the product chamber 144 without requiring ambient air to contact the product.

In a pressure-assisted embodiment, an interstitial chamber 192 is defined between the sleeve bag 140 and the inner surfaces of the outer container 102. A pressure port 194 communicates with the interstitial chamber 192 and permits introduction of a pressurizing fluid, such as compressed air, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, or another gas. Pressure applied to the exterior of the sleeve bag 140 urges product through the valve assembly 160 when the valve element 180 is opened. A pressure regulator, check valve, pressure-relief device, or rupture disk may be associated with the pressure port 194 or outer container 102.

The mating edge closures distribute internal loads around the periphery of the container portions and facilitate manufacture of the outer container without requiring insertion of the sleeve bag through a relatively small neck opening. The separable construction also permits inspection of the internally secured bag-to-valve connection before closure and, in reusable embodiments, permits replacement of the sleeve bag while retaining the container portions and valve assembly.

Although the illustrated valve assembly 160 is mounted in the first container portion 110, the valve assembly may be mounted in the second container portion, at the interface between the container portions, or in a separate closure component captured by the mating peripheral edges. Likewise, the sleeve bag may be free within the outer container except at the valve assembly, or may additionally be supported by tabs, ribs, hangers, guides, or releasable attachment points. These variations may be employed individually or in combination without departing from the scope of the disclosed container assembly.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in one patent-style paragraph, a dispenser in which complementary container halves form an enclosure and complementary cup halves hold an SBoV valve seat in place.
counterfactuals.output: A dispenser comprising: first and second complementary container halves coupled along respective peripheral edges to define an enclosure having a dispensing opening; first and second complementary cup halves disposed within the enclosure and joined to define a cup in fluid communication with the dispensing opening; and an SBoV valve seat positioned between the first and second cup halves, wherein cooperating retention surfaces of the cup halves engage opposing portions of the SBoV valve seat to capture and maintain the SBoV valve seat in a predetermined position and orientation relative to the dispensing opening, such that assembly of the container halves encloses the cup halves and assembly of the cup halves secures the SBoV valve seat without a separate seat-retaining fastener.
